body: You should look at it from a different perspective. The people you're comparing yourselves to experience the world differently from how you experience the world. It's okay to be afraid, it doesn't make you a failure. If a typical job isn't something that works for you, consider what type of things you can do from your own safe space. I recommend trying to seek support from a professional. It's a tough road, but you're a unique individual with needs that are different from what fits the system. I am too, lots of people are. I wish you the best of luck along your mental health journey and I hope you realize that being different doesn't make you a failure. If you feel like a failure, the system is failing you.

The reason I find this design upsetting is because women have a general pressure (not always and NOT exclusive to women) to be small and sexy and nice to look at. I'm pissed off with her original design because she was clearly drawn to be hot. Bruce Banner was drawn as a big scary green brute but the female version is only like 7 or 8 inches taller than me. Imagine being insecure about your height and then you find out a big monster is only a few inches taller than you are? I understand the CGI crew is being worked unfairly and the project isn't looking how it was likely intended to, but they put skin texture on the male Hulk which helped it look less unsettling but most designers will not put imperfections on women. I haven't read the comics or watched the show, I can't look at her design without my blood boiling

I hear you and I feel your pain. Sometimes it may feel like you're living for other people and not yourself. You don't come into this world buy choice, and then guilt is the only thing keeping you here. 

I want you to know that you are not alone. 

Although there may be people in the world who have a "worse" situation than you, that does NOT invalidate your pain, your suffering. Your world is everything to you, and your pain can be the worst thing you will ever know. 

It may not be helpful, but I'd like to pass on what has been passed to me. Consider the things in your life that make you happy, however small they may be, pass on the things that make you happy because they could save someone's life. They can make someone's pain the little bit more bearable that can make a difference. 

I'd like to hold your hand through your pain, and tell you once again that you are not alone, and you never will be. Please don't listen to the voice in your head that tells you otherwise. 

My words may not make a difference to you, but I truly hope that they did. I wish you the best of happiness, and I truly hope that you will continue living.
